tables.description: People who can place orders. Includes contact country, signup date, and whether the account is active.
A customer's order header. Links to the customer and optionally the sales rep (employee). Has a status and order date.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.desc: sales rep -> employees; NULL if none

columns.name: order_date
columns.desc: ISO date the order was placed

tables.description: Line items within an order: which product, quantity, the price captured at sale time, and a discount fraction. Revenue = quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount).

columns.name: unit_price
columns.desc: price per unit at time of sale

tables.description: Catalog of products with a unit price, category, supplier, and whether it is still active (not discontinued).
Product categories, optionally nested via parent_id (a category can be a subcategory of another).

columns.name: parent_id
columns.desc: parent category -> categories; NULL at top level

tables.description: Companies that supply products, with their country and typical lead time in days.

columns.name: lead_time_days
columns.desc: typical restock lead time; may be NULL

tables.description: Stock on hand per product: quantity available, the reorder threshold, and the warehouse. One row per product.

columns.name: reorder_level
columns.desc: restock when quantity falls below this

tables.description: Payments against orders, with amount, method, paid date (NULL if unpaid), and status.

columns.name: paid_date
columns.desc: ISO date paid; NULL if not yet paid

tables.description: Customer product reviews with a 1-5 star rating and optional text body.
Sales staff, with title, hire date, and a manager_id forming an org chart (self-reference).

columns.name: manager_id
columns.desc: this employee's manager -> employees; NULL for the top

_fewshot_note: These examples teach general SQL patterns over this schema (filter, join, group-by, having, order/limit, date range). They are kept DISJOINT from eval/gold.jsonl in both question and SQL, and deliberately do not reveal gold-specific constructs (the revenue formula, month bucketing, the reorder-level join, never-reviewed/never-ordered anti-joins, or the manager self-join) so the eval stays honest.

examples.question: List the payment ids that were made by wire transfer.
examples.sql: SELECT payment_id FROM payments WHERE method = 'wire';

examples.question: Show the review id and the email of the customer who wrote it.
examples.sql: SELECT r.review_id, c.email FROM reviews r JOIN customers c ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id;

examples.question: How many employees hold each job title?
examples.sql: SELECT title, COUNT(*) AS n FROM employees GROUP BY title;

examples.question: List the 3 cheapest active products by name and price.
examples.sql: SELECT name, unit_price FROM products WHERE is_active = 1 ORDER BY unit_price ASC LIMIT 3;

examples.question: How many customers signed up before 2023?
examples.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE signup_date < '2023-01-01';

examples.question: Which suppliers supply more than 3 products? Show supplier id and the count.
examples.sql: SELECT supplier_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM products GROUP BY supplier_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 3;
